text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had an episode of loss of consciousness; please stay calm while I ask you a few questions to determine the cause. Can you describe exactly what happened leading up to the fainting spell?

text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That episode of syncope immediately following urination is highly suggestive of micturition syncope. Did you experience any palpitations, chest pain, or shortness of breath before passing out?

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work confirms your glucose and electrolytes are normal, ruling out metabolic causes. Since your syncope occurred immediately after urination with a normal heart exam, this strongly points to a vasovagal event triggered by bladder emptying. Do you feel a sense of lightheadedness or urge to void right before these episodes happen?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope. The history of syncope occurring immediately after voiding, combined with a normal ECG and metabolic panel, and the absence of cardiac symptoms or neurological deficits, is classic for this benign vasovagal reflex.
